d9158272dd: Vowels can be stretched and carry the melody, so you can recognise a song from its vowels alone; consonants are short and have almost no pitch. Vowels are the body of singing, and consonants make the lyrics understandable.
a98540d68d: Consonants short and clear, vowels long and round
fde0cd78f7: Long notes almost always land on the vowel of the last word in a line. Keep the vowel round and the resonance can open up.
6ece0c0f76: Consonants come before vowels: make them clear the instant they leave your mouth, then hand straight over to the vowel.
2514c875f3: A song is a chain of notes, rhythms and harmonies. Trying to express emotion without a solid vocal foundation is like holding a gun that isn't loaded.
a836c027d7: Build2. The five basic vowels
ce7e2e0bfa: Guess the mouth shape first, then practise once in front of the mirror
5b773fc955: Jaw drops naturallyTongue tip resting lightly against the lower teeth. If the mouth opens wide but the throat doesn't, the sound actually goes flat.
2314e0c60e: Corners of the mouth spread slightly, tongue raisedKeep space inside the mouth; too flat or too pointed turns into a squeezed sound.
1f88e3a00c: Lips rounded and forwardLike a gentle whistle; watch that it doesn't get too quiet or muffled.
511b8c9ebb: Between [a] and [i]Jaw slightly open; don't let it blur into [i].
0c10ec69e1: Round lips, deep mouthLike holding an egg in your mouth; lips too loose turn it into [a].
